rationale: Interpreted the corrected revision and folded it into the shutdown account. All five declared comparisons now hold, including the two batched ones that were previously unresolved, so the account no longer rests on event values with an ambiguous admission: the unbuffered Barrier and Apply answer every post-shutdown call, VerifyLeader strands 11 of 24, and enabling BatchApplyCh - the option whose own comment says it buffers applyCh and breaks the Apply timeout guarantee - makes Barrier strand 11 of 24 and Apply 13 of 24. The mechanism is therefore demonstrated causally by a configuration change that alters nothing but the buffering. The existing Fact is extended under its own id with the corrected figures and the config-flip evidence, the interpretation is re-bound to the corrected experiment with its receipt cited, and the racing form recorded by the first receipt is kept as the timing-dependent manifestation that later runs did not reproduce.

knowledge.statement: VerifyLeader can hand back a future that nothing will ever complete, because the request waits in the buffered verifyCh that no reader drains once the run loop has exited and the future itself carries no shutdown channel to unblock on. The trigger does not require racing Shutdown: calls made after Shutdown has already returned strand about half the time, since the closed shutdown channel and a ready send into the buffered channel are both selectable. In the corrected revision, VerifyLeader answered 4, 4 and 5 of eight post-shutdown calls and left 11 of 24 futures incomplete, while the default unbuffered Barrier and Apply answered all 48 of theirs with ErrRaftShutdown. The same revision shows the mechanism by configuration: with BatchApplyCh, which buffers applyCh, Barrier answered 6, 3 and 4 of eight and Apply 3, 3 and 5, leaving 11 and 13 of 24 stranded. The first receipt shows the racing form as well, leaving 9 and 41 of 64 futures incomplete in two of three trials with none in the control; the two later revisions did not reproduce that form.
knowledge.conditions: Single-voter Raft instance, HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 50ms, in-memory transport in one process, BatchApplyCh off unless stated; 64 or 128 concurrent calls around Shutdown plus eight sequential calls after Shutdown has returned.
knowledge.changed_premise: The premise is unchanged and the evidence is extended: the earlier revision established the post-shutdown strand and attributed it to buffering, and this one confirms that attribution by configuration, since enabling BatchApplyCh makes the previously unaffected Barrier and Apply strand as well. The post-shutdown counts from the corrected revision replace the ones quoted from the ambiguous run, which carried the same values but unresolved comparisons.

interpretations.rationale: The question is whether a future handed back by VerifyLeader, Barrier or Apply around Shutdown can be left permanently uncompleted, and the corrected revision now answers it with all five declared comparisons satisfied, including the two that a configuration change makes decisive. A call made after Shutdown has returned should get the documented 'raft is already shutdown' error, and that is what happens for the unbuffered call kinds: Barrier and Apply answered all eight post-shutdown calls in every trial (comparisons 2 and 3, indices 3, 9, 15 and 5, 11, 17). VerifyLeader, whose channel is always buffered, answered only 4, 4 and 5 of its eight post-shutdown calls (indices 1, 7 and 13), leaving 4, 4 and 3 futures incomplete after 500ms. With BatchApplyCh enabled - the option whose comment says it buffers applyCh to MaxAppendEntries and thereby breaks the timeout guarantee on Apply - the two unbuffered kinds flip: Barrier answered 6, 3 and 4 of eight (indices 25, 29, 33) and Apply 3, 3 and 5 (indices 27, 31, 35), leaving 11 and 13 of 24 calls stranded respectively, with roughly half of the calls in each case answered and the rest left with a future nothing will complete (comparisons 0 and 1). That is a causal rather than correlational demonstration: the only difference between the answered and the stranded cases is whether the channel a future is sent to is buffered, since the call shape, the future type and the absence of a shutdown channel on these futures are identical. The source explains the split exactly: VerifyLeader and the apply path share the same select over the shutdown channel and a channel send, verifyCh is created with 64 slots while applyCh is unbuffered unless BatchApplyCh buffers it, and none of these futures sets ShutdownCh, so deferError.Error() waits on an error channel that no surviving goroutine will write. The repository's own test file records the same class as a TODO for these calls, which is an admission that the gap was known rather than a contract that permits a caller's Error() to block forever. The earlier receipts stay part of the account: the first showed the racing form, 9 and 41 of 64 futures incomplete in two of three trials with none in the control, and the two later revisions did not reproduce that form (0 of 128 per case), so the racing variant is a timing-dependent manifestation while the post-shutdown form is stable across three executions and is the one the claim rests on.
counterevidence: The racing form did not reproduce in the later revisions (0 of 128 calls per case in two runs), so the earlier 9 and 41 are a timing-dependent manifestation rather than a rate.

Without BatchApplyCh the apply path is never affected: Barrier and Apply answered every post-shutdown call in all three runs (indices 3, 9, 15 and 5, 11, 17 here), so the defect reaches the apply path only under a configuration whose own comment already warns that it breaks the Apply timeout guarantee.

Roughly half of the calls in each affected case are answered with the documented shutdown error rather than stranded, so the outcome is a per-call select choice, and no call that was answered carried a wrong outcome.
The repository's test file records the same class as a known TODO, which is evidence about intent, not a reason to treat an unbounded block as acceptable.
limitations: The post-shutdown counts per case come from three trials of eight calls each (VerifyLeader 11 of 24 stranded; batched Barrier 11 of 24; batched Apply 13 of 24), so they bound the mechanism rather than a population rate.
The strand is classified by a 500ms window; permanence is inferred from the source, since no reader of the affected channel remains and these futures carry no shutdown channel.
The batched cases use the default MaxAppendEntries as the buffer size, which never fills with eight post-shutdown sends, so blocking sends were not exercised.
Single-voter node, in-memory transport, 50ms timeouts, one process: no peer round trip or networked shutdown is involved.
interpretations.joint_history: This receipt is the fourth revision of one harness lineage: b2ccc787c9384b008b5f9c668746f760-experiment (64 calls, 1500ms window) gave the racing form, 49fa455b2fe94d53ab6fed2fad19ce33-experiment (128 calls, 4000ms window, post-shutdown phase) isolated the stable form, 3b7823e321e048b88feb0bab3b79b2bd-experiment added the BatchApplyCh cases, and 9bc3e6d5ea9c4b298e4a229e13b8f86d-experiment gave the batched cases distinct trial identifiers so their setup events admit them unambiguously. Event names, case kinds and field meanings are unchanged across the four.
